Maria: Heads up — saw a production OOM on a Dedicated pod during the overnight stress run, attaching short profile below.
Sam: link to logs?
Maria: `s3://perf-profiles/2034567890/oom-profile.pb` (repro snapshot). Quick summary: steady-state KV hit-rate ~72%, but allocator fragmentation climbs to ~38% after 2h of mixed short/long context traffic.
Jordan: That fragmentation number is really high. Is it mostly from mixed-size KV entries or from intermediate decode buffers?
Maria: Mostly KV entries. We saw a lot of small (~128B) entries and large (~64KB) entries interleaved. The slab allocator currently uses single pool with 512B slab size rounding.
Lee: So small entries are wasting 384B each, and large ones end up split across many slabs -> internal fragmentation + external holes when evicted.
Sam: Did the profile show peak workspace usage during prefill vs decoding?
Maria: Yes — prefill spikes allocate contiguous ranges then free quickly; decode allocations are more temporal but cause gaps because of our slab free-list behavior. I pasted the flame output excerpt: ```alloc: total 28.4GB
kv_data: 18.7GB (66%)
workspace: 6.2GB
fragmentation_overhead: 3.5GB (38% fragmentation)
peak_gpu_mem: 32.1GB
```
Jordan: Ouch. 38% frag on top of 32GB is bad. Suggestion: segregated pools by size class + implement per-request reserve cap to bound worst-case blowups.
Lee: Agreed. Two ideas we discussed earlier: 1) small-item slab pool (e.g., 256B slabs) for KV small entries; 2) a compact-on-evict background compaction that coalesces adjacent free slabs into larger spans. Both require changes to the allocator metadata though.
Sam: Can we prototype a fast path first: allocate two pools (small and large) and route KV entries by size threshold (e.g., <=1KB -> small pool). Avoid compaction initially. Measure improvement.
Maria: I ran a quick sim patch in user-space allocator earlier today. Results on replay workload: 
- baseline: fragmentation 38%
- two-pool routing (1KB threshold): fragmentation 19%
- p99 latency delta: +1.2ms (small increase due to pool lookup)
- OOM events: baseline 2 per 24h, two-pool: 0
So big win for two-pool.
Jordan: Nice. What about cache eviction interplay? If small pool fills, eviction policy might start evicting many small entries and churn. Need to ensure per-request caps to prevent single long request from flushing entire small pool.
Lee: For eviction, prefer LRU within each pool and per-request soft cap: request can consume up to X% of pool before being rate-limited. We already have global per-request caps for workspace; reuse that mechanism.
Maria: I added a per-request soft cap in the sim (20% of pool). That prevented single-request flushes and smoothed p99.
perfbot: Perf test run 2034568010 completed. Two-pool config improved steady token throughput by 4.7% and reduced mem-related tail failures to 0/1000.
Sam: Good sign. Next: kernel selection interaction — when we use int8 kernels for decode, memory layout changes slightly (packed activations), could that increase fragmentation?
Jordan: It might since quantized kernels reduce buffer sizes but change allocation alignments. We should run combined tests: two-pool + int8 kernels. Also check KV prefill vs decode ordering: prefill tends to allocate contiguous regions first, which helps; decode interleaving after prefill creates holes.
Lee: Operational idea: during heavy prefill bursts, temporarily route prefill KV allocations to a dedicated transient pool that aggressively evicts/compacts after the burst. That keeps long-lived KV entries separate.
Maria: I sketched a rollout plan: 
1) Implement two-pool allocator with size threshold and per-request soft caps (can be toggled via runtime flag).
2) Run cluster-wide canary on Dedicated fleet (10% capacity) for 48h with synthetic mixed workload.
3) If stable, enable on remaining Dedicated, then run Private rollout with opt-in.
4) Follow-up: implement background compaction if fragmentation stays >25% on any host.
Sam: Safety check: what about race conditions on compaction? We need pinned refcounts and KV entry relocation semantics. That's non-trivial.
Jordan: Yep. For compaction, we should only move cold KV entries (no active session refs). Implement relocation with write barrier: new slot allocated, copy GPU->GPU memcpy, update index atomically, then free old. Requires coordination with request path.
Maria: I'll add a perf test for relocation overhead; early estimate ~0.5-1ms per moved entry on NVLink nodes. We'll batch moves to amortize.
ops-bot: Incident link created: REDWOOD-3121 (OOM during overnight stress). Assigned to Maria, Jordan.
Sam: Action items: Maria to open PR for two-pool prototype (allocator + runtime flag). Jordan to spec eviction soft-cap and LRU per-pool. Lee to write canary plan and metrics (fragmentation %, mem headroom, p99 gen latency, eviction churn). I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to review PR and perf traces.
Maria: PR draft incoming in ~4h. Attaching the sim traces and the replay command we used: ```./replay --profile s3://perf-profiles/2034567890 --config experiments/two_pool.json --duration 2h```
Jordan: Thanks — will grab traces and start eviction spec.
Lee: Thumbs up. :thumbsup:
Maria: Thanks all, hoping this knocks down those random OOMs.
perfbot: Note: remember to tag experiments with model and kernel versions to make regressions traceable.
Sam: Good reminder. We'll include kernel and quantization tags in canary metadata.
Maria: End of thread.
